question:
A square is cut into three rectangles along two lines parallel to a side, as shown. If the perimeter of each of the three rectangles is \(24,\) then the area of the original square is

[Figure 1](figures/1989_AMC_12_Q03_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
All three rectangles have the same length, namely the side length of the square. Since their perimeters are also equal, their widths must be equal: subtracting twice the common length from each perimeter leaves twice its width.

[Figure 1](figures/1989_AMC_12_Q03_question_fig1.svg)

The three equal widths together span one side of the square, so each rectangle's length is three times its width. Half of its perimeter is its length plus its width, which is four widths. Therefore
\[
\text{strip width}=\frac{24\div2}{4}=3.
\]
The square has side length \(3\cdot3=9\), so its area is
\[
9\cdot9=\boxed{81},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).

solutionMethods.explanation:
Adding the rectangle perimeters counts the square's outside boundary once and each internal cut twice, because each cut belongs to two rectangles.

Let \(s>0\) be the side length of the square. Its outside boundary has length \(4s\). Each of the two cuts has length \(s\), so together they contribute another \(4s\) to the sum of the rectangle perimeters. Consequently,
\[
3\cdot24=4s+4s=8s,
\qquad s=72\div8=9.
\]
The square's area is therefore \(9\cdot9=\boxed{81}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutionMethods.label: Add the three perimeters
